title: I’ve been describing this show to friends as Kinky Boots meets In The...
transcript: Y'all are really sleeping on the show, and if you give me, like, a minute of your time, I will explain why you absolutely need to go see it. First and foremost, this show is so much more urgent than I expected it to be, which is to say that despite taking place in 1982 and being based on a movie from the early 2, it feels so of the present moment. I assume that this was mostly going to be a show around body positivity, and while that is certainly in there, it is much more about the American immigrant experience. It follows a group of largely undocumented immigrants and their struggles to just survive, make a living, all while avoiding deportation. And, yes, there are some serious moments, but it's also a musical comedy, so it's incredibly funny and fun. It has a really great Spanish infused score, really fun choreography, and one of the strongest books of a new musical this season. And I would love nothing more than to see the Broadway community rally around this show, because this is the type of show that really needs our support. It doesn't have any big, above the title celebrity stunt cast. Most of this cast is making their Broadway debut. It is technically based on a movie, but it's not a mega IP with a lot of brand recognition. And in a busy spring season with so many shows, it's really easy for a smaller show like This to get lost in the shuffle. So if you can, go see real women have curves. It is one of the best new musicals on Broadway right now, and I promise you, you will have a great time.
classificationReason: Key details—1982 setting, based on an early-2000s film, undocumented immigrant story, Spanish-infused score, Broadway debut cast—identify this as Real Women Have Curves. Creator advocates strongly for the show with specific opinions on score, choreography, and book, indicating first-hand attendance.
